summary: Comment-only. Option A of the WAL lane's proposal (no time bound on the swap window's hold; none can be added: the body runs uninterruptible calls and an early release is the hazard the window prevents). The docstring names the bounds (WINDOW_WAIT_S 60 s, _SWAP_HANDLE_WAIT_S 300 s shared by the restore and repair file steps, _RECHECK_S steps for waiting opens), what is unbounded (the first dispose_engine, one os.replace attempt, the encrypt body) and the measured hold of dispose_engine with a leftover log on the last connection (app engine, 4-core virtual disk, n 1-2: 0.88/0.98 s at 100 MiB, 0.7-2.6 s at 300, 5.6-8.1 s at 1,000; plain keeps other threads running, encrypted stops the whole process). Restore and repair fold the log before the window (frames between fold and window unmeasured). No behaviour change; A-029 stays leave + dispose.out.
